issue.title: sase-core's icon-field requirement for ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire breaks sase's provider specs (unreleased feature ahead of Python support)
issue.description:
sase-core commit 4f8c99e ('feat(artifact-ref): require icon field in provider ref spec wire'), which sits on sase-core's master after the 0.26.7 release tag (8bb76d1) and before commit 87e4a4f (needed for AGENT_SCAN_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION=6, added on sase's side in sase commit dc9da5576), makes the Rust artifact_ref_provider_spec_validate binding reject every ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire dict lacking an 'icon' field. sase's Python side has not been updated to supply 'icon' anywhere a provider spec is built: src/sase/artifact_providers/_builtin.py's builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec(), src/sase/sidecar_ref_config.py's _default_document_spec(), and multiple test fixtures across the suite.

REPRODUCTION (2026-08-13): with sase at master (dc9da5576) and sase-core rebased to its tip (87e4a4f, chronologically after the icon commit), 'just check''s test-scoped run failed 22 tests, all with 'ValueError: spec is not a valid ArtifactRefProviderSpecWire dict: missing field icon': tests/test_artifact_provider_registry.py (4 nodes, including completely generic registry-fixture specs unrelated to any real provider), tests/test_sidecar_ref_config.py (7 nodes), tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py (6 nodes), tests/agents_sync/test_referenced_by_planning.py, and tests/artifact_refs/test_context.py. Checking sase-core back out to 8bb76d1 (last commit before the icon requirement, still inside the sase-core-rs>=0.26.6,<0.27.0 floor) made all 22 failures disappear with no other changes.

IMPACT: any workspace whose sase-core linked checkout advances past the icon-field commit -- including via the documented 'sase repo open sase-core' recovery path that 'just install' itself recommends when it detects a stale wire schema -- will deterministically break the entire artifact-ref provider-spec validation surface, not just artifact refs specifically opted into icons.

SCOPE: add an 'icon' field (with a sensible default such as an empty string, or whatever default sase-core's Rust side treats as 'no icon') to builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec() and _default_document_spec(), and update any inline test-fixture provider specs the new requirement now rejects, so sase's Python side is coordinated with sase-core's icon-field feature before that feature reaches a released sase-core-rs version.

payload.entry: RELATED: sase-km — same class of sase-core/sase floor-coordination gap (a sase-core change lands without a matching sase-side update/floor bump), though the specific mechanism differs: sase-km is about the floor gate not knowing a required wire-schema minimum, while this bead is about an unreleased sase-core feature (icon field) landing on origin/master ahead of any coordinated Python-side support, so pulling past the floor via 'sase repo open' hits it even though the floor check itself passes.

Resolved by epic sase-kv, phase sase-kv.3 (sase commit d6a01e583 'feat(ace): add artifact tab icons'), which landed 2026-08-13T13:51Z -- after this bead was filed against sase master dc9da5576.

This bead reported the sase-core side of epic sase-kv (sase-core 4f8c99e, phase sase-kv.1) arriving ahead of its Python counterpart. Both halves are now on their repos' master, and the exact scope this bead asked for is implemented:
  - src/sase/artifact_providers/_builtin.py:21  builtin_plan_ref_provider_spec() declares ref.icon = '✎'
  - src/sase/sidecar_ref_config.py:398          _default_document_spec() declares ref.icon = DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_TAB_ICON ('◆')
  - inline test-fixture provider specs updated across the suite
  - src/sase/artifact_providers/registry.py:397 _ensure_compat_ref_provider_icon() injects '◆' plus a 'missing_ref_provider_icon' warning diagnostic for third-party plugin specs released before ref.icon, so an icon-less plugin degrades instead of being dropped

VERIFIED 2026-08-13 at sase master 7e4ac6d7c with sase-core-rs built from sase-core master f45e3b4 (v0.26.8, which contains the icon requirement): every test file this bead named passes -- tests/test_artifact_provider_registry.py, tests/test_sidecar_ref_config.py, tests/doctor/test_checks_config_repos.py, tests/agents_sync/test_referenced_by_planning.py, tests/artifact_refs/test_context.py = 37 passed. Full 'just test' = 29539 passed, 2 failed, both pre-existing and unrelated (sase-kw circular import; a monitor full-suite flake). 'just check' green on every lint gate.

The floor coordination the bead worried about is safe in both directions: pyproject pins sase-core-rs>=0.26.6,<0.27.0; a floor 0.26.6 core ignores the unknown 'icon' field (ArtifactRefProviderRefSpecWire sets no deny_unknown_fields), and a 0.26.8 core enforces it against a Python side that now always supplies it. That is the deliberate D2 decision recorded in plans:202608/artifacts_tab_icons.md and in a comment above ARTIFACT_REF_PROVIDER_SPEC_WIRE_SCHEMA_VERSION.

The broader 'sase-core feature lands ahead of coordinated Python support' concern stays with sase-km, which this bead already cites as RELATED.
